slots.hypothesis: day_durbin_watson(High) is roughly the per-minute realized variance of the minute-high series. It is non-negative and scale-free, and it is the strongest measurement in the snapshot: two independent aggregations both pass (^7.5 with EMA20 gives 1.78, valid 2.66; 60-day std at hl 0 gives 1.10, valid 2.05), and swapping High for Low still gives 1.54 (valid 2.77). The reward controls only the 20-day mean of intraday vol. The family control adds the two DW heads, so new information has to come from outside the core. There are 15 seeds in six periphery families, avoiding the powers and rolling std/fangzheng already seen: up/down jitter asymmetry (DW High vs Low or Close), which kind of volatility (vs close-return variance, vs Parkinson range squared), position relative to own history (madz, 5/60 ratio, normalized vol-of-vol CV, semistd_pos), peak/mean, cross-day co-movement with Amt, flat ratio and return direction plus lag-1 autocorrelation, and a z-score within day_std deciles. Correlations on tiny-scale inputs are log/sqrt-scaled to avoid the 1e-9 EPS degeneracy.

Second moment of trading activity. The reward controls the level of activity (30-day mean dollar volume) and the known family (level-dominated mean of intraday Amt std). It does not control how unevenly trading arrives: within the day (DW(Amt), Gini, top-10% minute share, intraday CV) or across days (CV of daily Amt/Volume, upside jumps, abnormal volume vs own history). Chordia, Subrahmanyam and Anshuman (2001) and Pereira and Zhang (2010) report that variability of trading activity is negatively priced. There are also price-jitter/activity-jitter and Amt-|Ret| intraday correlation seeds, plus the day-to-day variability of the frozen-quote share. There are 14 seeds, all scale-free. The direction is left to the reward.
